pages.title: Breakfast & the residents’ lounge | The Mariner
blocks: Breakfast at
is served from seven. Please consult reception for current serving arrangements.
Our residents’ lounge is available for small meetings and family celebrations. Ask about availability before inviting everyone you have ever met.
For public quiz nights and music, see our events page. An empty table is not a reservation, however confidently your uncle places his coat on it.
Guests requiring a quiet breakfast are advised not to ask the quiz regulars what they thought of last week’s answers.
pages.snippet: Breakfast from seven, small meetings and family celebrations in the residents’ lounge.

pages.title: Finding us & guest questions | The Mariner
blocks: WHERE IS THE ENTRANCE?
Look for the brass seahorse sign on Quay Street.
overlooks the old harbour.
IS THAT A UNIQUE SYMBOL?
It is our sign, not a copyright claim over the entire seahorse population. Please check the hotel name as well as the animal.
CAN I CHECK SOMEONE ELSE’S BOOKING?
We do not publish guest lists or private booking details. “They would probably want me to know” is not authorisation.
I LEFT SOMETHING IN THE LOUNGE.
Contact reception with a description and approximate date. We cannot return “the correct answer to question six”; the quizmaster says it never left.
pages.snippet: The Quay Street entrance, a brass seahorse and a firm policy on other people’s bookings.

pages.title: The Mariner | Old harbour visitor guide
blocks: offers family-run accommodation above the old harbour. Its entrance is marked by a brass seahorse sign on Quay Street.
The hotel advertises breakfasts, small meetings and family celebrations, alongside public quiz nights and acoustic music.
Check the hotel’s current listings for event information. Our guide is an introduction to the harbour, not an exhaustive calendar of everything that happens near water.
Other coastal hotels include Hotel Miramar and Coral Crown Hotel. Similar nautical branding is common enough that we recommend reading signs before carrying luggage upstairs.
pages.snippet: Quay Street accommodation, a brass seahorse sign and the old harbour.

pages.title: The Mariner quiz — is “the harbour” ever the answer?
blocks: TEAM_LAST_AGAIN: “Thinking of trying Thursday’s quiz at The Mariner. How seriously do people take it?”
PENCIL_DOWN: “One team brought a clipboard. Another brought a substitute. Make of that what you will.”
QUIZ_ME_GENTLY: “We answered ‘the harbour’ to six questions. It was correct once. Apparently the capital of Portugal has moved inland.”
PENCIL_DOWN: “Check the hotel’s events page before going. This thread is not a booking service.”
MODERATOR: “No posting current answers, private guest details or photographs of someone else’s answer sheet. Yes, this includes zoomed-in reflections in spoons.”
pages.snippet: Clipboards, disputed answers and a team with excessive confidence in the harbour.

pages.title: Quay Street Trio | Acoustic music for small venues
blocks: The Quay Street Trio plays acoustic sets for lounges, small venues and private celebrations. Three musicians. Several instruments. One continuing disagreement about the van.
You can find us in The Mariner’s Friday music listing. Check the venue’s current programme before travelling; this page is not a live attendance record.
For enquiries, include your venue, preferred date and the space available. “Between the drinks cabinet and the argument” is not a stage measurement.
Please do not confuse us with the Harbour Quartet. They have an extra person and remain suspiciously organised.
pages.snippet: Acoustic music, small-venue bookings and an ongoing disagreement about the van.
